A_target.statement:
Let $\gamma: \closedint 0 1 \to \C \setminus \set {z_0}$ be a [[Definition:Closed Curve|closed curve]].
Then its [[Definition:Winding Number|winding number]] $\map n {\gamma, z_0}$ is an [[Definition:Integer|integer]], and is invariant under [[Definition:Homotopy|homotopy]] in $\C \setminus \set {z_0}$.

B_source.statement:
Let $P$ be a closed [[Definition:Polygon|polygon]] not passing through $z_0$.
Then the signed angles subtended at $z_0$ by its edges sum to a multiple of $2 \pi$.

substitutions.the vertices of the polygon: sample points along the curve, with mesh tending to zero
substitutions.the signed angle increment at a step: the change of argument along that piece of the curve
substitutions.the total turning of the polygon: the total change of argument along the curve

derived.the sum being a whole number of turns: the winding number is an integer
derived.stability of the sum under small vertex: invariance of the winding number under deformation

object_map.reformulation: Replace the continuous change of argument by a finite sum of angle increments along a fine sampling.

validity_conditions: Each angle increment must be taken in the range between minus and plus half a turn, which is possible once the mesh is fine enough that consecutive samples subtend a small angle at the point.
The polygonal total is unchanged under further refinement, since splitting a step splits its increment additively, so the value is independent of the sampling.
The curve must avoid the base point, or the angle is undefined at some sample and no increment can be assigned.
proof_plan:
By [[Definition:Uniform Continuity|uniform continuity]] of $\gamma$, choose $0 = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_m = 1$ such that each $\map \gamma {\closedint {t_{k - 1} } {t_k} }$ lies in a disk not containing $z_0$.
Then consecutive samples subtend a small angle at $z_0$.

Sum the signed angle increments:
:$\displaystyle \Theta = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^m \map \arg {\frac {\map \gamma {t_k} - z_0} {\map \gamma {t_{k - 1} } - z_0} }$
using the principal argument.

Inserting a point between $t_{k - 1}$ and $t_k$ splits one increment into two whose sum is unchanged, as both lie in the same disk.
Hence $\Theta$ does not depend on the subdivision, only on $\gamma$.

By the source result, $\Theta \in 2 \pi \Z$; define $\map n {\gamma, z_0} = \dfrac \Theta {2 \pi}$.
A small deformation of $\gamma$ changes each increment continuously, so $\Theta$ changes continuously in $2 \pi \Z$ and is constant.
Hence the winding number is homotopy-invariant.
{{qed}}
